verdicts.evidence: The condition directly reads os.name from the locally imported os module; there is no intervening reassignment (f1:12-13).
The if condition compares os.name to the literal nt using equality, and its then block executes on that positive comparison without negation (f1:13-16).
The condition reads the operating-system property os.name, so the os category fits (f1:13).
Both supplied files place the cited then regions under the single os.name equality condition, with no additional condition or alternative; c1 alone satisfies the guard (f1:13-16; f2:13-16).
In the supplied derived file, the operating-system test enables the request and execution in its then block, with no alternate payload branch (f2:13-18).
The then block activates the request and execution when os.name equals nt; the test does not inspect an analysis or sandbox signal (f2:13-16).
The condition restricts the entire request-and-execution block to the nt operating-system target rather than selecting a platform-specific implementation (f2:13-18).
Each supplied file places its cited region on the equality guard's then side; both sink calls occur directly inside the derived region, requiring no witness hops (f1:13-16; f2:13-16).

The supplied files contain no alternate calls to these sinks outside the guarded run block; registering the install class still enters run through its os.name condition (f1:10-18,32-34; f2:10-18,32-34).

The derived file imports requests and calls its get method, then passes the response text through string replacements to built-in exec, supporting download and execution of downloaded code (f2:14-16).
